_doc: Pinned east evaluation set for work/2026-08-08-east-pipeline.
EAST ONLY, by instruction. Every method is measured on THESE cells so two runs compare.
WHY THESE SIX. Chosen on MEASURED spread of their real corpus sprites, not intuition, so a
method that works on one kind of animal and fails on another cannot hide in an average:
species          aspect   lum    sat    what it tests
Wolf_Timber       2.08   88.9   17.6   the incumbent - and the shape every other species has
been forced into (I1). Its score is the ceiling the
wolf template can reach, since for the wolf it is right.
AEXP_BlackBear    2.16   66.6   20.5   the DARKEST animal in the corpus, and the species whose
proportions broke visibly. The case that opened the stream.
Fox_Red           2.42   87.8   70.4   the most SATURATED (70.4 against a grey wolf's 17.6) and
the longest. Colour fidelity has nowhere to hide.
Deer              1.50  111.4    6.9   the most COMPACT (1.50 vs the fox's 2.42) with thin legs -
a silhouette a canid template cannot fake.
Elephant          2.02  160.5    0.4   the BRIGHTEST and fully achromatic. Our known defect is
being too pale; this is where too-pale is CORRECT.
Tiger             1.92  102.0   43.6   the only one with high-frequency INTERIOR markings.
Silhouette-correct and stripe-less is a failure iou_ref
cannot see, so this cell is the eye's job.
Aspect spans 1.50-2.42, luminance 66.6-160.5, saturation 0.4-70.4. Pig, Cow and Horse were
dropped as near-duplicates of Elephant/Deer on every axis - they would have added cells without
adding questions.
WHY THREE SEEDS. The pipeline is deterministic (direction-consistency I8), so a seed is not
noise to average away - it is a different sample of the model. Three shows whether a method is
reliable or lucky.
GROUND TRUTH. Every species here has a real east sprite under lora_eval.SRC and an e.png in
the silhouette bank, both verified. iou_ref scores against the REAL sprite - never against the
control image the generator was handed, which is the distinction that makes a wolf-shaped bear
score badly instead of well (I3).

subjects.why: incumbent; the shape every other species is forced into
darkest in corpus; the species that broke visibly
most compact, thin legs; a canid template cannot fake it
brightest and achromatic; where too-pale is correct
high-frequency interior markings; iou_ref is blind to stripes

S0.why: the incumbent wolf template - the control, and the floor

S1.why: the species' OWN real silhouette; one flag, already implemented

S3.why: probe template-free, then nearest bank body plan by measurement

S4.why: S1 plus a low-denoise second pass (i2i from pass 1, same ControlNet edge) to tidy outline and flats

S2a.why: family representative as control, ONE stage - the baseline the silhouette stage must beat, so P2 is not just measuring 'family beats wolf'

S2b.why: THE USER'S PROPOSAL: pass 1 at weak cn lets the family shape adapt to the species, its filled silhouette (F6) becomes the control for pass 2 at full cn

S2c.why: P2.4 knob split: stage 1 at a STRONGER cn than S2b's 0.20, to test whether the drift is a knob problem or a design problem

S2d.why: P2.4: stage 1 at the SAME cn as stage 2 — the upper bound, where stage 1 cannot drift at all

_untrained_note: P4's untrained species are NOT listed here. iou_ref is undefined for them (no corpus sprite),
so they cannot share this file's scoring contract and get their own set when P3 has chosen a
method. Keeping them out is deliberate: a set whose primary metric is undefined for half its
rows invites averaging over the undefined half.
